items.title: Drone Hits Tank at Libyan Refinery, Threatening Oil Facilities
items.author: Sherif Tarek and Hatem Mohareb
items.content: <article>A drone attack on an oil refinery in western Libya destroyed a storage tank, putting oil facilities at risk and potentially aggravating fuel shortages in the OPEC nation.</article>

items.title: NZ National Party to Meet as Leadership Pressure Mounts on Luxon
items.author: Ainsley Thomson
items.content: <article>New Zealand’s governing National Party will hold a meeting tonight as speculation mounts that its lawmakers are trying to remove Prime Minister Christopher Luxon as leader less than three months before a general election.</article>

items.title: Brouillette: Strait Control Is Iran's "Nuclear Weapon"
items.content: <article>Former US Energy Secretary Dan Brouillette says Iran's ability to control traffic through the Strait of Hormuz gives Tehran powerful leverage, arguing that control of the waterway is "in fact, a nuclear weapon." Brouillette says ships are not moving through the Strait at normal levels despite President Donald Trump's assertion that it is open, and warns prolonged disruption could establish a higher floor for oil prices because of the added risk premium. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on the late edition of Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Congress Has Power to Set AI Guardrails: Vogel
items.content: <article>Miriam Vogel, president and CEO of EqualAI and co-author of Governing the Machine, says Congress has the power to establish guardrails and accountability frameworks for companies using artificial intelligence as increasingly autonomous systems raise questions about human oversight. She speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on the late edition of Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Conley: Trump 'Does Not Have Many Options' on Iran
items.content: <article>Heather Conley, Senior Fellow at the American Enterprise Institute and Former Deputy Assistant Secretary of State, says dwindling targets and munitions are limiting President Donald Trump's options on Iran as hardliners in Tehran toughen their position. Conley says "nothing has shifted on the ground" in the Strait of Hormuz, with little traffic getting through, and argues Iran continues to view the waterway as a key source of leverage. She speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on the late edition of Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Markets Open the Week Flat as Oil Prices Rise | The Close 8/10/2026
items.content: <article>Bloomberg Television brings you the latest news and analysis leading up to the final minutes and seconds before and after the closing bell on Wall Street. Today's guests are Rithholtz Wealth Management Chief Market Strategist Callie Cox, Needham Senior Analyst Ryan MacDonald, Former Kansas City Fed President & CEO Thomas Hoenig, Kayne Anderson Rudnick Portfolio Manager, Senior Research Analyst Julie Biel, Founder ETFs Partner and Portfolio Manager Michael Monaghan, Evercore ISI International Political Affairs & Public Policy Chief Strategist Sarah Bianchi, Gotham Greens CEO Craig Stevenson, & Former NFL Linebacker Bart Scott. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Burnham Touts Plans to Crack Down on UK Vaping, Betting Shops
items.author: Joe Mayes
items.content: <article>Andy Burnham is detailing plans to crack down on the number of new vaping and betting shops, his latest announcement focused on tackling everyday issues as he tries to win over voters since becoming Britain’s prime minister.</article>

items.title: Jones Act Relief Extended, Iran War Presses On | Bloomberg Businessweek Daily 8/10/2026
items.content: <article>President Trump extended a waiver Monday for foreign ships transporting oil around the US as the war in Iran continues to disrupt supply chains. Bloomberg News' Mike McKee & Bloomberg Economics' Chris Kennedy explain the implications. Then, Grindr CEO George Arison discusses how the app is transforming to an AI-native platform. Plus, US Antimony Chairman & CEO Gery Evans discusses his company's work with the Trump Administration as it works to boost the US weapons stockpile and supply of critical minerals. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Michigan Senate Race Sets Stage for Midterms and 2028
items.author: Nancy Cook
items.content: <article>Will progressives become power brokers in the next presidential election?</article>

items.title: Turkey Passes Law to Achieve Peace With Kurdish Separatists
items.author: Murat Oztaskin and Selcan Hacaoglu
items.content: <article>Turkish lawmakers adopted legislation laying out the dissolution of a Kurdish separatist group and paving the way for one of the world’s longest insurgencies to come to an end.</article>

items.title: Trump Wants to Split Up the MMR Vaccine
items.content: <article>President Donald Trump signed an executive order to recommend breaking up the combined measles, mumps and rubella vaccine into three separate shots and overhauling the national childhood vaccination recommendations. He speaks in the Oval Office.  (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Trump Downplays Talks With Warsh Amid Fed Independence Doubts
items.author: Josh Wingrove and Courtney Subramanian
items.content: <article>President Donald Trump played down the frequency and length of his conversations with Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh, which raised fresh questions about whether he was seeking to directly influence the central bank.</article>

items.title: Trump Signals Restraint on Iran | Balance of Power 8/10/2026
items.content: <article>On the early edition of Balance of Power, Bloomberg Washington Correspondent Joe Mathieu discusses the latest from the Middle East. On today's show, Democratic Congresswoman Suzan DelBene of Washington, Stonecourt Capital Partner Rick Davis, Harvard Kennedy School Ash Center Visiting Democracy Fellow Jeanne Sheehan Zaino and Princeton University Professor Bernard Haykel. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Trump Ready to Let Economic Pressure Build on Iran
items.content: <article>President Donald Trump says he's ready to let economic pressure build on Iran. He also says the country should pay for damages it has caused to neighbors. Bloomberg's Josh Wingrove reports from the White House. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Democrat Candidates Aren't 'Cookie Cutter,' Says DCCC Chair DelBene
items.content: <article>Representative Suzan DelBene, who heads the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee, said Democratic candidates aren't 'cookie-cutter' and that they reflect their communities and the issues that matter to voters in their home districts. DelBene said that the path to winning back the house runs through purple districts around the country and that candidates running in those districts have 'crossover appeal.' (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Can Trump Influence the Federal Reserve and Interest Rates?
items.author: Enda Curran
items.content: <article>Since the start of his second term, President Donald Trump has waged a fierce campaign to impose his will on the Federal Reserve, breaking with the modern convention of walling off the US central bank from political interference, at least publicly. He sought to pressure Jerome Powell, the Fed chairman Trump appointed during his first presidential term, to cut interest rates. And he has attempted to push another Fed governor, Lisa Cook, from her job.</article>

items.title: Trump Makes Sweeping New Demands on Iran as Deal Hopes Dim
items.author: Josh Wingrove and Patrick Sykes
items.content: <article>US President Donald Trump made sweeping new demands on Iran after Tehran reiterated requests for reparations as part of talks to wind down the conflict, dimming hopes of a quick deal that would reopen the vital Strait of Hormuz as oil prices surged once again.</article>

items.title: Russia Bars Anti-War Yabloko Party From Parliamentary Elections
items.author: Bloomberg News
items.content: <article>Russia’s Supreme Court blocked the Yabloko party from appearing on the ballot in September’s elections to the lower house of parliament, effectively banning one of the country’s few political blocs openly calling for an end to the fighting in Ukraine.</article>

items.title: Trump Extends Narrowed Waiver of US Jones Act Shipping Mandates
items.author: Jennifer A. Dlouhy
items.content: <article>President Donald Trump has extended a waiver allowing foreign ships to transport oil and other commodities around the US for 90 more days, albeit with new limits, as the war in Iran disrupts crude flows and hikes fuel costs.</article>

items.title: Trump Wins Permission to Remove Brand Damage From BBC Suit
items.author: Erik Larson and Zoe Tillman
items.content: <article>President Donald Trump won permission to revise his $10 billion defamation lawsuit against the British Broadcasting Corp. by excluding his earlier claim that a 12-second clip in a documentary caused massive financial damage to his business.</article>
